analysis:
Examined both supplied .github/workflows/ci.yml excerpts and the change-range map. HEAD lines 17–25 introduce push-only cache saving and sparse checkout; lines 57–93, 163–197, 226–260 and 466–500 restore/check/save .git. Checkout explicitly disables credential persistence, and docs uses a separate full-history cache family. git fsck checks object connectivity, not the trustworthiness of cached configuration or hooks; no supplied evidence establishes attacker-controlled cache contents reaching a trusted branch, so this is not a supported finding. HEAD lines 266 and 509 pass save-caches into the provider build action; lines 400–418 restrict audio-cache writes while retaining fixture preparation as the test prerequisite.
BASE lines 529–893 were examined for native correctness, cache-hash, cluster metadata, build-cache and aggregate-gate interactions. These CI changes do not visibly alter prompt encryption, cache account scoping/at-rest protection (A-001, T-008, T-041), serving authorization (A-016, T-052–T-054), billing or privileged-helper authority. No concrete security regression is established in this scope.
Integration must verify the modified provider-ci-build action's save-caches and restored-build validation contracts, cache scoping/runner workspace isolation, and the remaining changed workflow sections beyond HEAD line 537, including cluster cache writes and aggregate gates. Those implementations are not supplied here; fsck alone must not be treated as provenance validation. Review the cross-file cache/documentation changes for effects on artifact identity and qualification (A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034, T-054).
